canonical_topic: Common oil market terminology: Brent Crude, Feedstock, Fuel Oils, Heating Oil
definition: A glossary of common oil-market terms: Brent Crude (a light, sweet North Sea crude oil used as an international pricing benchmark), Feedstock (any crude oil entering a refinery), Fuel Oils (liquid fuels heavier than gasoline, classified into six numbered categories), and Heating Oil / No. 2 Fuel Oil (essentially diesel fuel, the second-largest fraction of a refined barrel after gasoline).
core_idea: These are standard reference terms used throughout oil trading: Brent as a global benchmark grade, feedstock as the generic term for refinery input crude, and fuel oils/heating oil as classifications of refined output by weight and flow characteristics.
key_points: Brent Crude is a light, sweet crude oil from the North Sea that serves as an international pricing benchmark
Feedstock refers to crude oil of any type entering a refinery
Fuel oils are liquid fuels heavier than gasoline, classified into six numbered categories, with lower-numbered oils flowing more easily than higher-numbered ones
The two most common fuel oil categories are No. 2 fuel oil (diesel) and heavy oil (No. 4 to No. 6 fuel oil)
Heating oil (No. 2 fuel oil) is essentially diesel fuel and is the second-largest fraction of a barrel of crude oil after gasoline
Most crude oil types yield roughly half as much heating oil as gasoline when refined
relationships: Feedstock is the input to refining; fuel oils and heating oil are refined outputs
